the study of the metabolism and function of dehydroepiandrosterone (DHA) and its metabolites.
the measurement of the adrenal steroid hormone, DHA-S, in the serum of normal individuals and patients with adrenal disorders.

the dehydroepiandostrone sulphate levels are elevated in patients with untreated congenitual adrenal hyperplasia, in patients with a tumour in the adrenal cortex, in patients with adrenal hyperplasia of the adult, in patients with Cushing's disease, and in patients with C-19 steroid-producing tumours of the ovary.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

dehydroepiandostrone sulphate levels in serum are a useful index of the secretion rate of adrenal androgen, and that the method of radioimmunoassays provides a convenient and accurate means for its measurement.

we have established a radioimmunoassays for the estimation of dehydroepioandosterone sulphate in serum, and that the levels of the steroid in normal subjects and in pathological states, are consistent with the hypothesis of a major role for this steroid in the regulation of adrenal androgen function.

the radioimmunoassays for dehydroepiandrostenedione and dehydroepi-androstenedione sulphate are useful in the investigation of the adrenal androgen secretory status of patients with suspected adrenal disease.

we have a new method of assessing adrenal function in children and adults.
